entries.final_answer: Derive the cap from measurement. Operator guidance (batch-11 D1 brief): measure first, do not just raise the number; a cancellation must not read as a failure. Measured: p95 20.3 min = 102% of the 20-min cap; fixed costs (whole-tree collection ~8 min, serial wall-clock policy scan ~3.5 min on PRs) are architectural -- tests/ci/test_corpus_blocking_home.py requires tree-wide corpus reach and tests/ci/test_contracts_routing.py requires exactly one pytest invocation, so a path shard would weaken the lane. Fix: record the measured max suite in the repo's #5378 headroom form, derive the cap with ceil((max+0:30)*1.5) = 31, extend the cap guard to enforce it for this job, and make a budget expiry read as INCOMPLETE-advisory rather than a failed test (#4437). Selection semantics, deselects, continue-on-error and trigger stay unchanged.

Confirm the approach: derive the cap from the measured max with the repo's #5378 formula and make a budget expiry legible as INCOMPLETE (#4437), documenting why sharding is ruled out -- or shard the corpus selection by path and edit the two pinned guards?

entries.final_answer: Derive the cap from the measured worst case with the repository's existing #5378 headroom formula, record the derivation on the job, extend the guard that already owns the formula to this job, and make a budget expiry legible as INCOMPLETE/advisory via a step budget below the job cap plus a notice step. Reject the path/matrix shard: two live guards pin tree-wide corpus reach and a single pytest invocation. See plan.md Summary and IC-01..IC-04.

entries.final_answer: Known risks: the cap guard's block parser is indentation- and neighbour-sensitive (headroom line must sit directly above the job-level timeout-minutes); a step budget at or above the job cap is dead config; the recorded max can drift from reality (the 75% rule forces a cap bump when it grows); editing the suite step could accidentally change the selection (the recorded diff is the check). See plan.md IC-01..IC-03 Risks and WP01 Risks & Mitigations.
